definitions.explanation: A proposed change to an existing law, regulation, or plan. Commonly encountered in political and legal news.

examples.japanese: {改正案|かいせいあん}が{提出|ていしゅつ}された。
{憲法|けんぽう}{改正案|かいせいあん}について{議論|ぎろん}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Debate continues over the constitutional amendment.

examples.japanese: {与党|よとう}は{労働法|ろうどうほう}の{改正案|かいせいあん}を{国会|こっかい}に{提出|ていしゅつ}し、{来月|らいげつ}の{採決|さいけつ}を{目指|めざ}している。
examples.english: The ruling party submitted a labor law amendment to the Diet, aiming for a vote next month.

notes:
A compound of {改正|かいせい} (revision/amendment) and {案|あん} (plan/proposal). Very common in news about politics and legislation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {改正案|かいせいあん}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する: to submit a revision bill
- {改正案|かいせいあん}が{可決|かけつ}される: a revision bill is passed
- {改正案|かいせいあん}を{審議|しんぎ}する: to deliberate on a revision bill
- {憲法|けんぽう}{改正案|かいせいあん}: constitutional amendment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {修正案|しゅうせいあん}: amendment — changes to a bill already under discussion
- {法案|ほうあん}: bill — a proposed new law (not necessarily a revision)
- {改正|かいせい}: revision — the act itself, not the proposal
